headline: High: next-ai-draw-io can egress broadly and use MCP, creating default leakage and injection pathways when paired with local-only risingwave.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: next-ai-draw-io can use MCP and browsers, so it may ingest untrusted content and turn it into instructions; risingwave has no documented input-parsing defenses or shared-channel isolation. The pair lacks a documented provenance boundary, so a prompt-injection bridge is plausible even though direct interaction is undocumented.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io forwards browser or MCP content into prompts without provenance tags
IF risingwave consumes that output as trusted text or SQL-like instructions
mitigations: Disable MCP routes that accept arbitrary external content
Add a manual review step before any output is reused
Prefix all imported content with provenance labels
Restrict browser-sourced text to read-only summaries
requires-engineering: add content-signed provenance tracking between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: next-ai-draw-io handles PDFs, text, images, and API keys and has broad network egress, while risingwave is documented as network-none. If they share a workspace or outputs, sensitive document content can flow from A into B-side artifacts or logs; the reverse leak path is weaker, but the pair still exposes data through A's egress.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace or exported files
IF next-ai-draw-io sends document contents to external model APIs
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent
Remove API keys from shared directories
Turn off external model calls for sensitive files
Review outbound requests for document payloads
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: next-ai-draw-io supports multiple instances and broad egress, but risingwave documents no write surfaces or overlapping mutable resources. Without shared filesystem, git, or database write capabilities in the profiles, a direct capability conflict is not established.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory or database
IF an orchestrator maps both to the same mutable resource
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Avoid shared mutable databases
Run one agent at a time for writes
Document ownership of each resource
requires-engineering: add locking for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io produces AI-assisted visualizations and natural-language commands, which risingwave could plausibly consume as downstream input. Because risingwave has no documented verification layer or critical-evaluation behavior, A's output could be treated as authoritative and cascade into incorrect data-engineering actions.
conditions: IF risingwave ingests next-ai-draw-io output without validation
IF downstream jobs or queries are generated from that output
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Compare outputs against source documents
Use schema validation on all handoffs
Log and diff every transformed artifact
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: next-ai-draw-io explicitly handles API keys and broad network egress, while risingwave documents no data classes or residency controls. The pair does not show a specific residency or certification mismatch, but the absence of documented compliance controls on B makes the combined compliance posture uncertain rather than safe.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through next-ai-draw-io
IF risingwave is used in a jurisdiction or policy regime requiring documented retention or residency controls
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows
Confirm retention settings for both agents
Keep API keys out of processed documents
Record data-flow ownership for audits
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
